title: Check tire pressure and tread
summary: Low pressure and worn tread are the most common tire faults. Check pressure cold, compare with the door sticker, and inspect tread and sidewalls.
author: Ustad built-in

steps.title: Tires cold
steps.say: Check tires cold: parked for a few hours or driven only a short way.
steps.why: Driving heats the air inside, so hot tires read higher than they really are.
steps.safety: Park on flat ground away from traffic, hazard lights on.

steps.title: Find the right pressure
steps.say: Read the recommended pressure on the driver's door-frame sticker.
steps.why: The number on the tire sidewall is the MAXIMUM, not the right pressure for this car.

steps.title: Measure
steps.say: Remove the valve cap, press the gauge firmly on the valve and read it.
steps.why: A hissing gauge means it's not sealed and the reading will be low.
steps.must_show: a pressure gauge pressed onto the tire valve with a readable reading

steps.title: Adjust
steps.say: Inflate or release air to the sticker pressure, then measure again.
steps.why: Under-inflated tires overheat, wear the edges and make the car pull to one side.

steps.title: Check tread
steps.say: Check the tread. Replace the tire if it is level with the wear bars.
steps.why: Wear bars sit at about 1.6 mm, a common legal minimum. Below it, braking in the wet gets much longer.

steps.title: Check the sidewall
steps.say: Look along the sidewall for bulges, cuts or cracks.
steps.why: A bulge means the inner cords are broken. The tire can burst.
steps.safety: Bulge or deep cut: do not drive far. Fit the spare and replace the tire.
steps.must_show: a close, clear view of the tire sidewall

steps.title: Finish
steps.say: Refit the valve caps and repeat for all four tires and the spare.
steps.why: The cap keeps dirt and moisture out of the valve so it does not leak.

quiz.question: Why measure tire pressure when the tires are cold?
options: Hot tires read higher than they really are
The gauge only works when cold
quiz.explain: Heat expands the air, so a hot reading hides under-inflation.

quiz.question: Where do you find the right pressure for the car?
options: The number on the tire sidewall
The driver's door-frame sticker or owner's manual
quiz.explain: The sidewall shows the tire's maximum; the car maker's sticker shows the right pressure.

quiz.question: You find a bulge on the sidewall. What does it mean?
quiz.explain: Broken inner cords let air push the rubber out; it can burst.
